hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `H` only to get `n • AddMonoidHom.id X₀.toAffine.Point ≠ 0` for `n > 0`, via `H.nsmul_id_ne_zero'`. `compEnd'` and `image_kernelIdealSet_eq` are a subtype construction and a set-image rewrite whose bodies never use `H`. The fact can be proved without `H` or any characteristic assumption. Pick a prime r ≥ max n (ringChar κ) + 1 (Nat.exists_infinite_primes). If (r : κ) = 0, then ringChar κ ∣ r (ringChar.spec), so ringChar κ is 1 or r. It is not 1 (CharP.ringChar_ne_one, since κ is a field) and it is not r because r > ringChar κ. So (r : κ) ≠ 0. Then exists_addOrderOf_eq_prime_of_isAlgClosed gives a point R of order r, and n • R = 0 would force r ∣ n with r > n > 0, which is impossible. Everything else in the proof needs only `[IsAlgClosed κ]`, `[DecidableEq κ]`, `[X₀.IsElliptic]`, `[E.IsElliptic]` and the explicit binders.

It is used only inside `nsmul_id_ne_zero'`, to show that a prime r ≠ q' has (r : κ) ≠ 0. The ringChar argument replaces this: take a prime r > max n (ringChar κ); then ringChar.spec and CharP.ringChar_ne_one give (r : κ) ≠ 0. The rest of the proof is unchanged, and `Hyp` does not require this instance.

It is used only inside `nsmul_id_ne_zero'` (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Fact.out). That step can be replaced by the ringChar argument (ringChar.spec, CharP.ringChar_ne_one), which needs no assumption on q'. `Hyp` does not need this instance to elaborate.
